title: Sabouraud Dextrose Agar

references.label: Difco & BBL Manual of Microbiological Culture Media

purpose: Supports the growth of fungi (yeasts and molds) while its relatively low pH and high dextrose content discourage growth of many bacteria, particularly when combined with an added antibacterial supplement.

reference.label: Difco & BBL Manual of Microbiological Culture Media

preparationSummary: Suspend the dehydrated powder per the manufacturer's stated concentration, heat with agitation to boiling to fully dissolve, then sterilize and pour while still liquid. Antibacterial supplements (e.g. chloramphenicol or gentamicin), when used, are typically added after autoclaving once the medium has cooled.

sterilization.value: commonly autoclaved at 121°C for 15 minutes; some formulations recommend a shorter cycle to limit caramelization of the high dextrose content

storage: Refrigerate prepared plates in sealed bags.
expectedAppearance: Pale, translucent to slightly opaque agar before inoculation.
qualityControl: Verify growth support with a known fungal reference organism (e.g. Candida albicans or Aspergillus niger, per institutional protocol) and, where an antibacterial supplement is used, verify inhibition of a bacterial control.

reactions.reaction: Smooth, creamy colonies, typically within a few days
Characteristic colony texture, color, and growth pattern that varies by genus, often requiring longer incubation
Growth is discouraged by the low pH and, where added, actively inhibited by an antibacterial supplement

manufacturerNotes: Plain SDA (without an antibacterial supplement) is not strongly selective against bacteria on its own — supplemented variants (e.g. Sabouraud Dextrose Agar with chloramphenicol) are commonly used when bacterial overgrowth is a concern, and formulations vary between manufacturers.
